tools.name: get_insider_activity
tools.description:

their role (CEO, CFO, Director, 10% owner…), and a link to each filing. Use for questions like
'are insiders buying or selling NVDA?' or 'show Tesla insider trades this year'.

tools.name: find_insider_buying
tools.description:
Scan ALL U.S. companies for insider open-market PURCHASES — the strongest insider signal. Ranks companies by
total value bought, number of distinct insiders buying ('cluster buying'), or recency. Use for 'which insiders
are buying right now?', 'CEO purchases this month', 'companies where 3+ insiders

tools.name: get_insider_signal

tools.name: get_insider_person

Find an insider (executive, director, or large holder) by name and list their open-market trades across all
companies, with totals. Use for 'what has Warren Buffett bought recently?' or 'Jensen Huang stock sales'.

tools.name: search_companies

Look up tickers and official company names (with SEC CIK) from recent insider filings. Use when the user
names a company but not its ticker, or a ticker returns no results.

tools.name: get_data_status
tools.description:
Report what data CapitalSnitch covers, how fresh it is, update schedule, sources, and known limitations.
Use when asked 'how current is this?', 'what data do you have?', or before making time-sensitive claims.

The alert and daily-briefing emails CapitalSnitch sent the user recently, newest first (Edge plan). Use for
'what alerts did I get today?', 'did anything trigger on my watchlist?'. Never counts toward the daily limit.

tools.description:
Facts about CapitalSnitch itself: what it is (a live commercial service, not a demo), every plan with price,
daily limit and features, which data each plan includes, payment methods, how to sign up (right here in the chat
or on the website), which AI apps can connect and how, and the support email.

tools.description:
The user's own CapitalSnitch account: plan (Free / Scout / Analyst / Edge), whether it is active, renewing,

Step 2 of 2: checks the emailed code, creates the account (or signs in), and returns the user's personal

tools.description:
Has the payment arrived and is the plan active? For crypto, pass order_id: shows waiting / seen on the network
/ confirmed. For card, omit it: shows the account's current plan. Free to call.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_congress_trades, manage_watchlist, get_my_alerts, get_my_account, get_account_link, start_signup · Private data: get_dilution_history, find_insider_clusters, get_congress_trades, about_capitalsnitch, get_my_account, get_account_link · Public sink: get_dilution_history, get_institutional_ownership, manage_watchlist, set_alert_preferences, about_capitalsnitch, get_my_account, get_account_link, start_signup, buy_plan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_congress_trades, manage_watchlist, get_my_alerts, get_my_account, get_account_link, start_signup · Private data: get_dilution_history, find_insider_clusters, get_congress_trades, about_capitalsnitch, get_my_account, get_account_link · Public sink: get_dilution_history, get_institutional_ownership, manage_watchlist, set_alert_preferences, about_capitalsnitch, get_my_account, get_account_link, start_signup, buy_plan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
